units.title: Unit 1: What is AI Really?
units.description: Demystify AI, Machine Learning, Tokens, Context Windows, and Hallucinations.
units.stampDescription: Mastered the core mechanics of AI, LLMs, and Tokenization.

lessons.title: AI vs Human Intelligence
lessons.description: Learn what Artificial Intelligence is—and what it isn't.

questions.question: What is Artificial Intelligence (AI) at its core?
choices: A conscious digital mind that thinks like a human
Computer systems designed to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence
A giant database that remembers every website on the internet
A magic search engine that writes code automatically
questions.explanation: AI refers to computer systems engineered to recognize patterns, make decisions, and process language—simulating capabilities previously limited to human minds.

questions.question: True or False: Generative AI models genuinely feel emotions and possess self-awareness.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: Generative AI models are mathematical pattern matchers. They predict output based on probability, without feeling, consciousness, or personal beliefs.

questions.question: Identify the flawed statement in this student's summary:
questions.scenario: "AI models understand the meaning of life because they have read every philosophy book written."
choices: AI cannot read philosophy books at all
Reading text gives AI statistical word patterns, not true conscious comprehension or understanding
AI is only used for math calculations
Philosophy books are kept secret from AI training
questions.explanation: Processing text allows AI to predict related words with high accuracy, but it does not equate to human-like sentience or true comprehension.

questions.question: Complete the statement about AI capabilities:
questions.codeOrPrompt: AI excels at rapid pattern recognition and text generation, but humans excel at genuine ____ and empathy.
choices: calculator speed
critical reasoning
data storage
pixel display
questions.explanation: Critical reasoning, ethical judgment, and emotional empathy remain uniquely human strengths that complement AI tools.

questions.question: Which of these is the best description of Generative AI?
choices: Software that copies and pastes existing Wikipedia articles
AI models capable of creating new content like text, code, images, and audio based on learned patterns
A physical robot that cleans houses
An algorithm that strictly filters spam emails
questions.explanation: Generative AI generates brand-new original media (text, music, images, code) by predicting plausible sequences learned from vast datasets.

lessons.title: Machine Learning & LLMs
lessons.description: Discover how Large Language Models learn from massive text datasets.

questions.question: What does 'LLM' stand for in modern AI?
choices: Linear Logic Machine
Large Language Model
Linked Learning Matrix
Logic Language Method
questions.explanation: LLM stands for Large Language Model—a deep learning model trained on vast amounts of text to understand and generate human language.

questions.question: How does an LLM decide which word comes next when writing a response?
choices: It looks up an exact pre-written answer in its memory bank
It calculates the highest statistical probability for the next piece of text based on its training
It rolls a random digital dice with no logic
It asks a human operator in real time
questions.explanation: LLMs predict the most likely next token (word or word fragment) given all the preceding text in the prompt and conversation context.

questions.question: True or False: Machine Learning models require explicit step-by-step programming for every single answer.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: Unlike traditional software with hardcoded rules, Machine Learning algorithms learn patterns directly from example data.

questions.question: Spot the common misconception about LLMs:
questions.scenario: "Gemini is connected directly to my brain and knows what I am thinking before I type."
choices: Gemini requires keyboard or voice input and processes text signals, not brainwaves
Gemini uses satellite radar to read minds
LLMs only work when plugged into power outlets
Gemini is a physical entity that stands next to you
questions.explanation: LLMs only process explicit input provided through text, audio, or image prompts.

questions.question: Which sentence best explains 'Machine Learning' to a 10-year-old?
choices: Machine learning is gradient descent over high-dimensional tensor weights.
Machine learning is teaching a computer by showing it thousands of examples instead of writing rigid rules.
Machine learning is storing files on a cloud drive.
Machine learning is installing updates on your smartphone.
questions.explanation: Comparing ML to learning from examples is clear, relatable, and accurate without overwhelming technical jargon.

lessons.title: Tokens & Context Window
lessons.description: Understand how AI breaks down text and how much memory it can retain.

questions.question: What is a 'Token' in the context of Large Language Models?
choices: A physical coin used to pay for AI services
A basic chunk of text (like a word, part of a word, or punctuation) processed by the model
A security password used to login to AI apps
A digital image generated by DALL-E
questions.explanation: Tokens are the fundamental building blocks of AI language processing. In English, 1 token is roughly 4 characters or 0.75 words.

questions.question: What is an AI's 'Context Window'?
choices: The size of the chat box on your laptop screen
The maximum amount of tokens (prompt + history) the AI can consider at one time
The time of day when AI servers run fastest
The brightness setting of your AI application
questions.explanation: The context window is the AI's short-term working memory capacity. Anything outside this limit is forgotten or truncated.

questions.question: True or False: If a conversation exceeds the context window limit, the AI may forget details mentioned earlier in the chat.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: When context limits are reached, earlier messages fall out of the active window, causing the AI to lose track of earlier constraints.

questions.question: Estimate token usage:
questions.codeOrPrompt: A paragraph of 100 English words will typically equal roughly ____ tokens for an AI model.
questions.explanation: As a rule of thumb, 100 English words equal approximately 130 to 140 tokens because long words and punctuation get split into multiple tokens.

questions.question: Arrange how AI processes a user's prompt in order:
choices: User sends text prompt
Text is converted into numerical tokens
Model calculates probability for response tokens
Tokens are converted back into human-readable words
answer: Text is converted into numerical tokens
Model calculates probability for response tokens
Tokens are converted back into human-readable words
questions.explanation: This pipeline—Tokenization -> Statistical Processing -> Detokenization—is how all modern transformer-based LLMs operate.

lessons.title: Training & Inference
lessons.description: Learn the difference between training an AI model and running inference.

questions.question: What happens during the 'Training' phase of an AI model?
choices: The AI chats live with millions of users every second
The model processes massive datasets over weeks to adjust billions of internal connections (weights)
Engineers manually write answers to every question in the world
The computer downloads new RAM memory from the internet
questions.explanation: Training is the computationally heavy phase where a model learns language patterns from massive datasets.

questions.question: What does 'Inference' mean when using AI?
choices: Searching the web for news stories
The process where a trained model generates an answer to a user's specific prompt
Deleting old AI models from cloud servers
Translating code from Python to JavaScript
questions.explanation: Inference is the live execution phase—when you type a prompt into Gemini and receive a generated response in real time.

questions.question: True or False: Every time you ask Gemini a question, it updates its base core training weights permanently.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: Standard inference is read-only. Chat responses use existing weights and context memory without modifying the base model weights on the fly.

questions.question: Identify the key term:
questions.codeOrPrompt: A model's knowledge cutoff date refers to the moment its ____ dataset was finalized.
choices: Inference
Training
Tokenization
Web Browsing
questions.explanation: An AI's baseline knowledge ends at its training data cutoff date unless supplemented with real-time tools like Google Search.

questions.question: Spot the inaccurate technical claim:
questions.scenario: "I trained a model locally on my laptop by typing 3 messages into ChatGPT last night."
choices: 3 messages in chat is inference context, not full model weight pre-training
ChatGPT runs on smartphones, not laptops
Chat messages convert to images automatically
Models can only be trained during full moons
questions.explanation: Providing chat examples sets short-term context during inference. Pre-training models requires thousands of GPUs and petabytes of data.

lessons.title: Hallucinations & Limitations
lessons.description: Recognize why AI makes up facts and how to spot errors.

questions.question: What is an 'AI Hallucination'?
choices: When the AI generates colorful artwork
When an AI confidently presents incorrect or fabricated information as factual truth
When the server crashes due to high traffic
When the AI refuses to answer a question
questions.explanation: Hallucination happens because LLMs predict plausible-sounding text patterns rather than looking up verified truth databases.

questions.question: Which of the following is a classic AI hallucination risk?
choices: Asking the AI to summarize a provided article text
Asking the AI to invent a fiction story about a dragon
Asking the AI for exact legal citations or historical quotes without providing source material
Asking the AI to translate 'Hello' to Spanish
questions.explanation: Asking for specific citations, statistics, or quotes from memory often leads to realistic-looking but fabricated references.

questions.question: True or False: If an AI states a fact in a confident, authoritative tone, it is guaranteed to be 100% accurate.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: AI models match tone patterns learned from professional text, sounding equally confident whether they are correct or hallucinating.

questions.question: What is the best strategy to prevent AI hallucinations when doing research?
choices: Tell the AI: 'Never lie to me under any circumstances.'
Provide reliable reference documents and ask the AI to restrict answers strictly to the provided text
Ask the same question 50 times in a row
Type the prompt in ALL CAPS
questions.explanation: Grounding the AI in verified source material (RAG or document context) drastically reduces fabricated answers.

questions.question: What is the Golden Rule of AI Literacy when using AI for important tasks?
choices: Trust everything the AI says without checking
Verify critical facts, statistics, and sources independently
Only use AI between 9am and 5pm
Never share your name with an AI model
questions.explanation: Always verify high-stakes information (medical, financial, legal, academic) with authoritative primary sources.

units.title: Unit 2: Prompt Engineering Fundamentals
units.description: Learn to write clear, structured, contextual prompts that get exceptional results.
units.stampDescription: Mastered clear instructions, context, constraints, and few-shot examples.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a Perfect Prompt
lessons.description: Discover the 4 key building blocks of every effective prompt.

questions.question: Which 4 elements make up a highly effective prompt structure?
choices: Greeting, Sign-off, Password, Link
Task Instruction, Context, Constraints, Output Format
Code, Database, Server, API Key
Title, Header, Footer, Page Number
questions.explanation: Providing a clear Task, relevant Context, boundaries (Constraints), and desired Format yields superior AI responses.

questions.question: Which prompt is significantly better for getting a good email draft?
choices: Write an email about the project meeting.
Draft a polite 3-paragraph email to my manager updating her on the Website Redesign project. Mention we finished design mockups and need approval by Thursday.
Send an email to my team right now.
Email project updates quickly.
questions.explanation: The second prompt clearly defines audience (manager), tone (polite), length (3 paragraphs), key details (finished mockups), and deadline constraint (Thursday).

questions.question: Spot the weakness in this prompt: 'Explain climate change.'
choices: It uses the word climate
It lacks target audience, length, focus area, and output tone
It is typed in English
It contains punctuation
questions.explanation: Vague prompts produce generic, encyclopedia-style answers. Specify whether you want a 5th-grade explanation, bullet points, or scientific summary.

questions.question: True or False: Adding politeness like 'Please' and 'Thank you' improves AI accuracy mathematically.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: While friendly language sets a pleasant tone in training data, clarity and specific instructions matter far more than social niceties.

questions.question: Fill in the missing prompt element:
questions.codeOrPrompt: Task: Summarize article. Context: For busy executives. Constraint: ____.
choices: Use bullet points under 100 words
Make it extremely long
Write in French
Add random emojis
questions.explanation: Setting length and structural constraints prevents rambling outputs and saves reading time.

lessons.title: Providing Context & Role
lessons.description: Guide the AI by assigning expert roles and background detail.

questions.question: What is 'Role Prompting'?
choices: Asking the AI to play an actor in a movie script
Instructing the AI to adopt a specific persona or expert perspective (e.g., 'Act as a Senior UX Designer')
Changing your profile picture on the AI app
Assigning admin permissions to the AI
questions.explanation: Assigning a role steers the AI toward specialized vocabulary, analytical depth, and industry standards learned during training.

questions.question: Select the strongest role-based prompt for feedback on a resume:
choices: Look at my resume.
Act as an expert Tech Recruiter. Review my resume summary for a Staff Software Engineer position and suggest 3 high-impact improvements using bullet points.
Is my resume good?
Fix all spelling mistakes on my resume.
questions.explanation: Specifying the role (Tech Recruiter), target position (Staff Engineer), and precise deliverable (3 high-impact improvements) yields actionable feedback.

questions.question: True or False: Providing background context helps the AI tailor its answer to your specific situation.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: Without context, AI relies on average assumptions. Context grounds the answer in your specific goals and audience.

questions.question: What is missing from this prompt? 'Act as a nutritionist and make a meal plan.'
choices: Nothing, it is 100% complete
Dietary restrictions, health goals, calorie needs, and timeline duration
The word 'Abracadabra'
A computer virus scan
questions.explanation: A meal plan requires key context parameters like allergies, budget, calories, and duration to be safe and helpful.

questions.question: Complete the role prompt formula:
questions.codeOrPrompt: Act as an experienced ____. My target audience is ____. Please explain ____ in 3 simple steps.
choices: Teacher / 10-year-olds / photosynthesis
Computer / printers / paper
Database / SQL / server
Window / glass / frames
questions.explanation: Matching the role to the target audience creates a perfectly calibrated explanation.

lessons.title: Setting Clear Constraints
lessons.description: Control length, style, tone, and negative constraints effectively.

questions.question: Why are constraints crucial in prompt engineering?
choices: They slow down the server so it costs less money
They prevent rambling answers and ensure the output matches your formatting and tone requirements
They force the AI to turn off security guards
They make the prompt look like code
questions.explanation: Constraints set boundary parameters (word count, tone, banned phrases, structure) that guide the AI's generation.

questions.question: What is a 'Negative Constraint' in prompting?
choices: Insulting the AI in the prompt text
Explicitly telling the AI what NOT to include (e.g., 'Do not use buzzwords like synergy or leverage')
Writing prompts when you are in a bad mood
Deleting bad prompts from history
questions.explanation: Negative constraints explicitly ban specific undesirable behaviors, terms, or formats.

questions.question: Which constraint instruction is most effective for a summary task?
choices: Make it brief.
Summarize the text into exactly 3 bullet points, keeping the total response under 60 words. Do not include intro banter.
Don't write too much text please.
Write a short paragraph or whatever.
questions.explanation: Quantitative constraints (3 bullet points, under 60 words, no intro banter) give the model clear measurable goals.

questions.question: True or False: Positive framing ('Do X') is generally more reliable than negative framing ('Don't do Y') in prompts.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: AI models focus on key nouns. Saying 'Keep explanation under 5 sentences' works better than 'Do not write long text'.

questions.question: Identify the constraint type:
questions.codeOrPrompt: Constraint: 'Format response as a markdown table with columns: [Feature | Pros | Cons]'. This is a ____ constraint.
choices: Structural
Negative
Temporal
Emotional
questions.explanation: Structural constraints dictate the visual and syntactic layout of the generated text.

lessons.title: The Power of Examples (Few-Shot)
lessons.description: Show, don't just tell! Use zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot examples.

questions.question: What is 'Few-Shot Prompting'?
choices: Asking 3 questions in a single second
Providing a few input-output examples in your prompt so the AI learns the exact pattern
Taking screenshots of AI responses
Running a prompt only 2 times
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting shows the model concrete examples of desired input -> output pairs, dramatically reducing errors.

questions.question: What is 'Zero-Shot Prompting'?
choices: Giving a prompt with zero instructions
Asking the AI to perform a task directly without providing any prior example demonstrations
Deleting all chat history before asking
Using an AI model with zero parameters
questions.explanation: Zero-shot relies purely on the AI's pre-trained knowledge without showing custom examples.

questions.question: Identify why this few-shot prompt works so well:
questions.scenario:
"Convert product names to SKU codes:
Input: Wireless Headphones -> Output: SK-WIR-01
Input: Solar Charger -> Output: SK-SOL-02
Input: Smart Watch -> Output:"
choices: It teaches the exact naming convention and pattern visually
It uses color highlighting
It is written in Python code
It uses complex calculus equations
questions.explanation: Showing pattern structure (prefix-category-number) guides the model to produce 'SK-SMA-03' effortlessly.

questions.question: True or False: Few-shot examples are especially effective for complex formatting and custom taxonomy tasks.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: Examples eliminate ambiguity when defining complex JSON schema, specialized classifications, or unusual writing styles.

questions.question: Order the steps to build a Few-Shot Sentiment Classifier prompt:
choices: Define the Task: Classify customer review sentiment
Example 1: 'Loved the fast shipping!' -> Sentiment: Positive
Example 2: 'Arrived broken and late.' -> Sentiment: Negative
New Target Input: 'Product is okay, but box was damaged.' -> Sentiment:
answer: Define the Task: Classify customer review sentiment
Example 1: 'Loved the fast shipping!' -> Sentiment: Positive
Example 2: 'Arrived broken and late.' -> Sentiment: Negative
New Target Input: 'Product is okay, but box was damaged.' -> Sentiment:
questions.explanation: Task -> Demonstration 1 -> Demonstration 2 -> Target Query is the canonical structure for few-shot prompting.

lessons.title: Iterative Refinement & Follow-ups
lessons.description: Treat prompting as a conversation. Refine, critique, and improve.

questions.question: What should you do if an AI's initial response is slightly off target?
choices: Give up immediately and assume AI cannot do the task
Provide a follow-up refinement prompt pointing out specific adjustments needed
Re-type the exact same prompt 10 times
Complain on social media
questions.explanation: Prompting is iterative! Refining through multi-turn follow-ups allows you to guide the output closer to perfection.

questions.question: Select the best follow-up prompt to improve an overly technical summary:
choices: Bad answer.
Great summary! Now simplify the language so a non-technical manager can understand it. Replace jargon with real-world analogies.
Start over from scratch.
Why did you write that?
questions.explanation: Acknowledging what worked while giving clear direction on tone/simplicity achieves immediate results.

questions.question: Spot the powerful follow-up technique known as 'Self-Correction':
choices: Asking the AI: 'Review your previous answer for potential errors or logical flaws, then output a corrected version.'
Deleting your original prompt and closing the browser tab
Telling the AI that it passed an exam
Asking the AI what time it is
questions.explanation: Prompting the AI to critique its own work activates self-evaluation patterns that catch subtle mistakes.

questions.question: True or False: It is often better to break a huge complex task into 3 sequential conversational steps than asking for everything in one massive prompt.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: Decomposing complex work into step-by-step subtasks maintains accuracy and prevents the model from missing requirements.

questions.question: Complete the effective follow-up prompt template:
questions.codeOrPrompt: Keep the content from section 1, but make section 2 more ____ and convert section 3 into a ____ table.
choices: concise / 2-column
loud / square
random / hidden
invisible / colorful
questions.explanation: Targeted feedback preserves good parts while specifying precise formatting upgrades.

units.title: Unit 3: Advanced Prompting & Strategy
units.description: Master System Prompts, Chain-of-Thought, Output Schemas, and Complex Decomposition.
units.stampDescription: Mastered system instructions, chain-of-thought, and output schemas.

lessons.title: System vs User Instructions
lessons.description: Learn how developers steer AI guardrails and persona behavior.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a 'System Instruction' in AI development?
choices: To display pop-up ads in the app
To set high-level rules, persona, boundaries, and formatting instructions that govern the AI's behavior across all user turns
To restart the server if it gets too hot
To charge credit cards for tokens
questions.explanation: System instructions establish foundational rules and behavioral guardrails prior to receiving user input.

questions.question: How does a 'User Prompt' differ from a 'System Instruction'?
choices: User prompts are written in code, system instructions are written in English
System instructions define global rules; User prompts contain specific runtime inputs and user queries
User prompts are secret and invisible
There is no difference between them
questions.explanation: System instructions guide the overall assistant persona, while User prompts supply dynamic questions and data.

questions.question: True or False: Well-crafted System Instructions help prevent AI from breaking character or violating safety boundaries.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: System instructions provide strong guardrails that prioritize developer specifications over adversarial user inputs.

questions.question: Which of these is the best example of a System Instruction for a Customer Support Bot?
choices: Hi, I want a refund for order #1234.
You are a calm, professional customer support agent for Acme Cloud. Answer user questions strictly using Acme policy docs. Never ask for credit card numbers.
Where is my package?
Tell me a joke about dogs.
questions.explanation: The second option sets persona (calm agent), company context (Acme Cloud), policy boundaries, and explicit safety constraints.

questions.question: Complete the developer system instruction:
questions.codeOrPrompt: System Instruction: 'Always respond in valid ____ format. Do not enclose in markdown blocks.'
choices: JSON
MP3
PNG
JPEG
questions.explanation: JSON system instructions allow software backends to parse AI responses automatically.

lessons.title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
lessons.description: Unlock advanced problem solving by encouraging step-by-step reasoning.

questions.question: What is 'Chain-of-Thought' (CoT) prompting?
choices: Linking multiple physical computers together with chains
Asking the AI to break down complex logic step-by-step before arriving at a final answer
Generating a chain of random words
Translating text into 5 languages sequentially
questions.explanation: Prompting 'Think step-by-step' forces the model to generate intermediate reasoning tokens, significantly boosting math and logic accuracy.

questions.question: Which phrase is famous for triggering Chain-of-Thought reasoning in AI?
choices: Give me the answer right now!
Let's think step by step.
Don't explain anything.
Guess the answer quickly.
questions.explanation: The magic phrase 'Let's think step by step' encourages the transformer model to allocate token space for deliberate logical steps.

questions.question: Why does Chain-of-Thought improve math and logic performance?
choices: It downloads a scientific calculator into memory
It allows the model to compute intermediate state tokens instead of jumping directly to a final token guess
It speeds up internet connection
It lowers screen brightness
questions.explanation: Since LLMs predict one token at a time, writing out intermediate calculation steps gives future tokens necessary context.

questions.question: True or False: In production user applications, you can instruct the AI to perform reasoning internally and present only the clean final summary to the user.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: You can use system instructions or response schemas to separate internal reasoning steps from user-facing responses.

questions.question: Order the logical steps for a CoT Word Problem solver:
choices: Identify given variables from problem statement
Write down formula or relationship equations
Calculate intermediate subtotals step-by-step
State final verified conclusion
answer: Identify given variables from problem statement
Write down formula or relationship equations
questions.explanation: Following systematic problem-solving phases eliminates compounding calculation errors.

lessons.title: Formatting AI Outputs
lessons.description: Master structured outputs: Markdown tables, JSON, Lists, and Codes.

questions.question: Why request JSON or Markdown format from an AI?
choices: Because AI cannot write normal sentences
Structured formats make data clean, scannable, and easy for software apps or spreadsheets to process
It makes the text print faster on paper
It reduces internet data usage
questions.explanation: Structured formats allow programmatic parsing by frontend components, databases, and automated workflows.

questions.question: Select the best prompt to request comparison data for 3 laptops:
choices: Compare 3 laptops.
Create a Markdown table comparing MacBook Air M3, Dell XPS 13, and Lenovo ThinkPad X1. Use columns: [Model | Price | Battery Life | Best For].
Tell me which laptop is best in a big paragraph.
Write laptop names.
questions.explanation: Specifying Markdown table format with exact column names guarantees a clean, side-by-side comparison.

questions.question: True or False: Providing a target JSON schema in your prompt helps ensure the AI generates valid keys and data types.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: Defining a key-value schema prevents missing fields and inconsistent formatting.

questions.question: Spot the issue in this prompt request: 'Give me JSON data but write conversational paragraphs before and after it.'
choices: Conversational fluff will break automated JSON parsers (`JSON.parse()`) unless isolated cleanly
JSON cannot contain numbers
Conversational text is illegal on web servers
AI cannot generate JSON
questions.explanation: When building API integrations, instruct the AI: 'Output raw JSON only. Do not wrap in markdown or conversational text.'

questions.question: Complete the output format constraint:
questions.codeOrPrompt: Format: Provide output as a bulleted checklist where each item starts with an emoji and a bold ____.
choices: Header Title
Page Number
Random Number
Secret Code
questions.explanation: Combining visual elements (emojis + bold headers) creates readable executive summaries.

lessons.title: Spotting AI Hallucinations
lessons.description: Develop critical auditing skills to verify AI claims and code.

questions.question: Read this AI-generated biography sentence and spot the red flag:
questions.scenario: "Albert Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for inventing the iPhone in Zurich."
choices: The year 1921 is incorrect
Einstein winning for inventing the iPhone is anachronistic and false (he won for the photoelectric effect)
Zurich is not a real city
Physics does not exist
questions.explanation: LLMs can combine real entities (Einstein, Nobel Prize, iPhone) into absurd, plausible-sounding historical fabrications.

questions.question: Which type of query carries the HIGHEST risk of AI hallucination?
choices: Summarizing text pasted directly into the prompt
Asking for specific hyper-niche academic citations, URLs, or precise legal case numbers from memory
Translating simple phrases into French
Formatting a list of names alphabetically
questions.explanation: Fabricating realistic-looking citations, book titles, and web URLs is one of the most common LLM hallucination patterns.

questions.question: True or False: Search Grounding (like Google Search in Gemini) helps dramatically reduce hallucinations for real-time events.
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: Grounding queries in live Google Search results provides factual web references to back up generated statements.

questions.question: What is the best prompt instruction to force the AI to admit when it lacks reliable information?
choices: Always make a guess if you don't know.
Answer based ONLY on provided sources. If the answer is not in the text, reply strictly with: 'Information not found in source.' Do not extrapolate.
Try your best to make up something plausible.
Search your imagination.
questions.explanation: Giving the model an explicit 'escape hatch' ('Information not found') prevents it from fabricating answers under pressure.

questions.question: Fill in the audit principle:
questions.codeOrPrompt: When using AI for medical, legal, or financial advice, the human must act as the ____-in-the-loop.
choices: Human
Robot
Algorithm
Database
questions.explanation: The 'Human-in-the-loop' paradigm ensures safety by having a qualified human review and approve AI outputs.

lessons.title: Mastering Task Decomposition
lessons.description: Break massive projects into structured, multi-step AI workflows.

questions.question: What is 'Task Decomposition' in AI prompt engineering?
choices: Deleting tasks from your calendar app
Breaking down a large, complex objective into smaller, manageable sub-prompts executed in sequence
Writing prompts in multiple languages at once
Allowing the computer to turn off automatically
questions.explanation: Decomposing complex goals (e.g. 'Build a marketing strategy') into discrete steps (Research -> Outline -> Draft -> Critique) yields higher quality results.

questions.question: Order the sequence to generate a complete Blog Post with AI:
choices: Prompt 1: Brainstorm 5 engaging article headline ideas based on target topic
Prompt 2: Create a detailed sub-heading outline for chosen headline
Prompt 3: Draft content section by section using research facts
Prompt 4: Review draft for tone, flow, and SEO keywords
answer: Prompt 1: Brainstorm 5 engaging article headline ideas based on target topic
Prompt 2: Create a detailed sub-heading outline for chosen headline
Prompt 3: Draft content section by section using research facts
Prompt 4: Review draft for tone, flow, and SEO keywords
questions.explanation: A multi-stage pipeline produces well-structured, coherent content compared to asking for a whole article in one blind shot.

questions.question: Spot the error in this single prompt attempt: 'Build me a full mobile app, write all code, market it on social media, and get me 1,000 paid users.'
choices: It combines too many distinct strategic, technical, and marketing tasks into one vague request
Mobile apps are illegal
Social media does not accept AI text
It uses the word 'app'
questions.explanation: Overloading a single prompt causes shallow, incomplete summaries. Each subtask deserves its own dedicated prompt pipeline.

questions.question: True or False: You have now mastered the fundamentals and advanced techniques of AI Literacy & Prompting!
choices: True
False
questions.explanation: Congratulations! By completing these modules, you are well on your way to becoming an AI Literacy Champion!

questions.question: Choose the most empowered mindset for your future AI journey:
choices: AI will replace my thinking entirely.
AI is a powerful co-pilot that amplifies my human creativity, critical thinking, and productivity when guided by great prompts.
AI is too complicated for regular people.
I should never use AI tools.
questions.explanation: Treating AI as a collaborative co-pilot unlocks incredible potential while keeping human wisdom at the helm.
